chunks: What Mūsā ibn al-Qāsim narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who performed the obligatory tawaf around the House, then did not know whether he had completed seven circuits or eight. He said: As for the seven, he is certain of them; rather, his doubt fell upon the eighth, so let him perform two rakʿahs.

key_terms.اسْتَيْقَنَ: he became certain; certainty is legally relied upon here
key_terms.الثَّامِنِ: the eighth circuit, which is the object of doubt
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: the two rakʿahs prayed after tawaf
key_terms.طَوَافَ الْفَرِيضَةِ: the obligatory tawaf required in the rite

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone doubts whether their obligatory tawaf was seven circuits or eight?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about doubt during the obligatory tawaf of the Kaʿbah. If a person is certain of seven circuits and only doubts whether there was an eighth, the seven are treated as established and he proceeds to pray the two rakʿahs of tawaf.
